summary: Practise banking cyber-control testing, evidence review and audit reporting. Explore the five-day course and build usable audit work products.
lede: Cybersecurity auditing in banking examines how security controls work across banking services, systems and data. For internal auditors, cybersecurity auditors and technology risk specialists, it develops practical skills in defining scope, mapping risks to controls, testing access and change evidence, reviewing incident records and documenting prioritised findings with traceable conclusions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who scope, execute or use cybersecurity audits in banking operations. It suits intermediate learners with experience in audit, information security, technology risk or banking systems who need a practical approach to control testing and evidence-based reporting.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of banking operations, information security, technology risk or internal audit is expected. No programming is required; exercises use audit scenarios, control records and evidence samples.
